name: send
synopsis: ssize_t send(int sockfd, const void *buf[.len], size_t len, int flags);
ssize_t sendto(int sockfd, const void *buf[.len], size_t len, int flags, const struct sockaddr *dest_addr, socklen_t addrlen);
ssize_t sendmsg(int sockfd, const struct msghdr *msg, int flags);
description: The send(), sendto(), and sendmsg() system calls are used to transmit a message to another socket. Send() is for connected sockets, while sendto() and sendmsg() can specify the destination address. No indication of failure to deliver is provided.

parameters.name: sockfd
parameters.description: File descriptor of the socket to send from

parameters.name: buf
parameters.description: Buffer containing the message to send

parameters.name: len
parameters.description: Length of the message in bytes

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags for the send operation (e.g., MSG_DONTROUTE)

parameters.name: addrlen
parameters.description: Length of the destination address for sendto()

parameters.name: msg
parameters.description: Message header structure for sendmsg(), including scatter/gather arrays and ancillary data

return_value.success: Returns the number of bytes sent
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: Write permission denied or attempt to send to a broadcast address as unicast
Another Fast Open is in progress
No peer address set for non-connection-mode socket
Message too long to send atomically
Socket is not connected and no target given
File descriptor does not refer to a socket
Local end shut down on connection-oriented socket

bugs: Linux may return EPIPE instead of ENOTCONN.
